paragraphs: You can give us the day-to-day running of your hotel, or bring us in for a single service while you keep running the property yourself. block.heading: Your questions before requesting a quote

items.question: Does the first call cost anything?
items.answer: No. The 30-minute consultation is free and comes with no obligation. Using your property's own figures, we'll estimate the net effect before you commit to anything.

items.question: How long does a quote take?
items.answer: Expect a reply within one business day, followed by a short call before we quote. Once we understand the work, we'll confirm the quote timeline with you. Hotels with more than 200 rooms, luxury properties and multi-property groups get a custom quote.

items.question: Do you need system access to quote?
items.answer: To begin, we work from your property details and whatever figures you share on the call. Please don't put passwords in your request. If some access turns out to be needed, we'll talk it through with you before you set it up.

items.question: Do I have to sign a long contract?
items.answer: Asking for a quote doesn't tie you to a contract. You'll get the proposed engagement length and terms to look over first, and only then agree them directly with our team.

items.question: Which properties do you take on?
items.answer: Hotels, motels, hostels, B&Bs, serviced apartments, short-term rentals and vacation rental portfolios. There's no minimum number of units.

items.question: Is there a long contract?
items.answer: That depends on the service. Each agreement sets its own initial period and notice terms, and you see them in writing before you sign.

items.question: How are fees set?
items.answer: That depends on the service: management is charged as a share of revenue or a fixed monthly fee, and revenue and OTA plans by room count. After a first call, you get the price for your property in writing before you commit.

items.question: Who handles on-site work?
items.answer: Anything that needs someone at the property is done by our partners or local contractors. Our own team is remote only.

items.question: How does the handover work?
items.answer: First we go over the agreed work with you, set up account and system access, and confirm your leadership contact. Access starts out read-only, and the plan and any major rate or budget changes need your sign-off.

items.heading: Advance billing and payment
items.text: Monthly fees are invoiced in advance at the start of each month, and payment is due within 15 days by ACH, international wire or credit card. Our prices are in USD, though you can pay in CAD, EUR or AUD at the exchange rate on the invoice date. A full management agreement also carries a one-time onboarding fee, separate from the revenue management setup fee.

items.heading: Included and third-party costs
items.text: Your fee pays for our team's time and our own pricing, reporting and BI tools. Third-party costs are billed to your property at cost, with no mark-up from us. These include your PMS, channel manager, other software subscriptions, OTA commissions, photographers and specialist partners.

items.heading: Taxes and transfer charges
items.text: USD prices don't include applicable sales taxes, and we add those only where the law requires it for your property's location. Your bank's transfer charges are yours to pay. Currency-conversion costs for payments in CAD, EUR or AUD are on us.

items.heading: Ending a plan
items.text: Once the three-month initial period is over, you can end your plan with 30 days' written notice, and there's no exit fee. The one-time setup fee can't be refunded after setup work starts, and we don't refund fees already paid for the current month.

items.heading: Pausing a plan
items.text: After the three-month initial period, you can also pause, again with 30 days' written notice. Monthly billing then stops for up to three months. You won't pay a pause fee, and if you restart within that time, you won't pay a new setup fee either.

items.heading: Changing plans
items.text: Upgrades take effect on the day you make the change, and the price difference is prorated for the rest of that month. Downgrades start from your next billing cycle.

items.heading: Results and refunds
items.text: Revenue results aren't guaranteed, and we don't offer refunds, because market demand, competitors and other outside factors all affect performance. What we do is work closely with you, check results against agreed targets on every monthly strategy call and change the strategy whenever a target is missed.

block.heading: Three properties: challenges, actions and results

items.heading: 32-room motel in Oregon, United States
paragraphs: Revenue management. Rates stayed the same most weeks, making quiet weekdays hard to fill and leaving busy weekends priced too low. We reviewed booking pace, historical occupancy and local demand remotely, introduced daily rates by room type and arrival date, adjusted minimum stays around busy weekends, and sent weekly performance summaries and pricing priorities. Over the first six months compared with the same six months a year earlier, occupancy rose from 58% to 69%, average daily rate increased 9%, and revenue per available room increased 30%.

items.heading: 46-room hotel in Ontario, Canada
paragraphs: OTA management. Inconsistent room descriptions and unclear cancellation terms on Booking.com and Expedia left the owner spending hours correcting availability and answering avoidable questions. We corrected listing details, amenities and policies, reorganised owner-supplied photos, aligned room mapping and availability, monitored listing performance, and handled OTA-related guest messages remotely. In month four compared with the month before takeover, Booking.com listing conversion rose from 2.1% to 2.8% and Expedia listing conversion rose from 1.8% to 2.3%. The owner's OTA administration fell from eight to two hours per week, comparing the weekly average in month four with the month before takeover.

items.heading: 28-room motel in Queensland, Australia
paragraphs: Full remote management. The owner handled guest messages, pricing and maintenance coordination without consistent handovers, leading to slow replies and missed follow-ups. We took over reservations, guest messaging and arrival instructions remotely, coordinated cleaning and maintenance with local contractors carrying out all on-site work, managed pricing and OTA availability through a shared operating calendar, and introduced weekly owner reports covering performance, outstanding issues and approval requests. In month six compared with the month before takeover, median guest-message response time fell from three hours to 24 minutes, and maintenance requests resolved within 48 hours rose from 54% to 87%. The owner's routine operational workload fell from 26 to six hours per week, comparing the weekly average in month six with the month before takeover.

paragraphs: Before handover or opening, we review your systems, staffing, contracts and permits, and we handle the licenses your hotel needs. Our [management and pre-opening services](/) need 6 to 8 weeks before handover or 3 to 6 months before opening, and we also give advice earlier, at the design stage. On the percentage fee, full management that includes revenue and OTA management is at the upper end of that range, and properties with more than 100 rooms are toward the lower end. The agreed percentage changes only when your services change.

rows: Performance measures
We measure revenue management by gains in market share and profit per booking. Chasing occupancy or rate on its own loses value when channel costs and competitors are overlooked.
Engagement scope
We include revenue management in our hotel management or provide it on its own. When it's standalone, pricing decisions have less influence over sales, distribution and on-property operations.
Dedicated service and pricing

Our [revenue management service](/revenue-management/) gives you daily pricing decisions, weekly occupancy, ADR and RevPAR reports, and dashboard updates every 24 hours. Monthly Base / Extended / Complete prices are set by room band: up to 20 rooms, USD 750 / USD 1,040 / USD 1,300; 21–50 rooms, USD 1,090 / USD 1,500 / USD 1,900; 51–100 rooms, USD 1,600 / USD 2,200 / USD 2,800; 101–200 rooms, USD 2,300 / USD 3,100 / USD 4,000. items.heading: Hiring decisions and timing
paragraphs: Before we start searching, we agree your budget and how you want sign-off to work. Within that budget, we hire with your general manager, unless you want to approve hires yourself. Once the search starts, hourly roles take 14 to 21 days and management roles take 30 to 45 days.

items.heading: Candidate and contract fit
paragraphs: We screen candidates for the skills each role needs and for a personality that suits your hotel. We recruit hourly, salaried and tipped employees on full-time, part-time, seasonal and temporary terms.

items.heading: Departments and seasonal preparation
paragraphs: We recruit across front desk, housekeeping, maintenance, food and beverage, and management. If your property is seasonal, we start 8 weeks before opening, so your team is ready on day one.

items.heading: Training and development
paragraphs: Your front-desk team completes six structured remote video sessions within the first 30 days of working with us. We also develop and support staff retention, deliver leadership development, and provide sales and marketing training and direction.

items.heading: Replacement recruitment
paragraphs: If someone we recruited resigns or is dismissed for performance within their first 90 days, we find you a replacement with no additional recruitment fee.

items.heading: Required pre-start checks
paragraphs: Before anyone starts, we check at least two employment references, the required licences and certificates (including food-handling or first-aid credentials), and their right to work under your country’s rules. All of these checks are finished within 5 business days of the offer.

items.heading: Conditional background screening
paragraphs: Where local law permits it and your candidate consents, we arrange background checks through licensed local screening providers, and your property is billed at cost.

items.heading: Full hotel management
paragraphs: With [third-party management](/), we run an independent hotel’s daily operations remotely while you keep ownership. We recruit, onboard, orient and train your General Manager and Director of Sales, including brand immersion when it’s required.

items.heading: Qualified project oversight
paragraphs: Our [project management](/project-management/) team is made up of PMP-certified managers with construction experience and carries professional liability insurance. We send you the insurance certificate before you sign.

items.heading: Your contracting authority
paragraphs: We act as your agent, not as the builder. You sign contracts directly with contractors and vendors. We review the bids and, where needed, select or recommend providers.

block.heading: Data-Driven Assessment of Your Current Operations
paragraphs: We assess how your property runs today using benchmarking, reporting and technology for upgrading your systems.

steps.heading: Share operating records
steps.text: You give us read-only access to 12 months of P&L statements, PMS reports, payroll and timekeeping records, maintenance and work-order logs, and guest reviews and complaint logs, along with your current vendor contracts.

steps.heading: Rebuild missing baselines
steps.text: If your labour, maintenance or guest-service records are incomplete, the assessment still goes ahead. We rebuild baselines from payroll exports, vendor invoices and online reviews. We mark the less precise findings as estimates that show direction, not exact figures.

steps.heading: Assessment fee
steps.text: You pay a fixed assessment fee. It rises with your room count, your revenue outlets and the number of systems we connect beyond your PMS and channel manager. Rebuilding missing records also raises the fee.

steps.heading: Extra scope
steps.text: Analysing more than 3 years of history costs more, and so does reviewing several properties together. If your hotel has more than 200 rooms, you get a custom quote.

steps.heading: Establish complete tracking
steps.text: We don't hold back the assessment until your records are perfect. Instead, we set up tracking while we diagnose, which gives you 90 days of complete data for the follow-up review.

steps.heading: Identify recovery priorities
steps.text: Our [recovery diagnosis](/receivership/) examines your financial health, market position, physical condition and operating performance. We trace revenue, cost, staffing and brand-compliance problems to their causes. Then we define corrections and repositioning opportunities specific to your property.

block.heading: Project Timelines, Budgets & Monthly Cost Reporting
rows: PIP timeline
4 to 8 months from appointment to closeout. About 2 to 3 months of that is pre-construction.
Full renovation timeline
9 to 15 months, of which 3 to 5 months is pre-construction.
New-build timeline
18 to 30 months, of which 6 to 12 months is pre-construction.
Pre-construction
These periods include design, permits, pricing and procurement.
Total project budget
Your budget covers hard construction costs; architect, engineer and consultant fees; permits and connections; FF&E, OS&E and IT; pre-opening costs; and construction-period financing.
Contingency
We set aside 10% of hard costs for new builds and 15% for renovations at operating hotels. No draw happens without your prior written approval.
Budget and schedule
We give you both at appointment and track performance against them throughout. When a budget line is forecast to exceed its allowance by more than 5%, we flag it for your approval.
Monthly reporting

You get a written cost report, a dashboard and a monthly owner report. Together they show approved budgets, signed-contract and purchase-order commitments, actual spending, forecast cost to complete and the funding still required. You can also view the dashboard live.
Cost accountability
We track committed, forecast and contingency costs by budget line, programme and property, and we link every cost change to the decision behind it.
Progress reporting
Our reports cover schedule progress, critical-path milestones, open risks and every approved or pending scope change. Between monthly reports, we send you a short weekly progress email.
Closeout documents
You receive PDFs of the as-built drawings, operation and maintenance manuals, warranties, guarantees, contractor final releases, final cost reconciliation and the completed punch list.
